_comment: THE CLINICAL CONTRACT. Owned by R3 (Abhigyat). Defines the ICDR scale, the referable-DR endpoints, and the operating-point rules. Phase 3 and Phase 6 code MUST read endpoint definitions from this file rather than hardcoding a threshold, so that the definition used to produce a number is always recoverable from git history. See docs/clinical_definitions.md for the reasoning and citations.
_change_policy: Endpoint DEFINITIONS below are frozen as of Phase 0 and must not change after Phase 3 training begins. Numeric operating-point THRESHOLDS are null until Phase 3 selects them on the validation split; once written they are frozen by commit and must not be re-tuned. Messidor-2 must not be read before both are frozen (project hard rule 1).

_amendments.summary: Fixed an ENCODING bug, not a definition change. v1.0.0 expressed referable DME as the literal 'dme_grade >= 2', which is IDRiD's 0/1/2 scale. Messidor-2's adjudicated_dme is binary 0/1, so the clause matched nothing there and the primary endpoint silently degraded to the DR-only secondary - wrong number, right label, no error raised. Replaced the dataset-specific integer with a semantic predicate (dme_referable) plus a per-dataset encoding map. The clinical meaning of 'referable DME' is unchanged, so this is permitted under the change policy and lands before Phase 3 begins.
_amendments.why_the_scales_are_equivalent: Both datasets use the SAME clinical criterion - hard exudates within 1 optic disc diameter of the fovea/macula centre - they just encode it differently. IDRiD spreads it over 0/1/2 (grade 2 = within 1 DD); Krause et al. collapsed it to a binary referable flag for Messidor-2. Verbatim from Krause et al.: 'hard exudates within 1 disc diameter was considered referable DME', and the Messidor-2 (their 'Validation') set 'used a standard of hard exudates within 1 DD of the fovea'. So IDRiD==2 and Messidor-2==1 denote the same finding.

icdr_scale._source: International Clinical Diabetic Retinopathy Disease Severity Scale (Wilkinson et al., Ophthalmology 2003)

dr_grades.2: Moderate NPDR - more than MA only, less than severe
dr_grades.3: Severe NPDR - 4-2-1 rule, no proliferative signs
dr_grades.4: Proliferative DR - neovascularization or vitreous/preretinal haemorrhage

dme_grades._source: IDRiD 'Risk of macular edema' column. Graded by shortest distance from the macula centre to any hard exudate.
dme_grades.1: Hard exudates present, all further than one optic disc diameter from the macula centre
dme_grades.2: Hard exudates within one optic disc diameter of the macula centre (clinically significant macular oedema risk)

dme_encoding._comment: B12 fix. 'Referable DME' is ONE clinical finding - hard exudates within 1 optic disc diameter of the fovea centre - but each corpus encodes it on its own scale. Resolve dme_referable through this map; NEVER compare a raw DME integer against a literal threshold, because the same integer means different things in different datasets. A dataset absent from this map has no DME labels: the primary endpoint is NOT scoreable there and code must fall back to secondary_dr_only EXPLICITLY and say so in the output, never silently.
dme_encoding.criterion: Hard exudates within 1 optic disc diameter of the fovea / macula centre.
dme_encoding.shared_limitation: Both corpora use hard exudates as a PROXY for DME rather than OCT - Krause et al. name this as a limitation of their own reference standard. Our Module 2 derives DME the same way (exudate mask + fovea + disc diameter), so our method matches the reference standard's method. State the proxy when reporting DME numbers.

idrid.note: Grade 1 = hard exudates present but FURTHER than 1 DD from the macula - present but NOT referable. Do not treat >=1 as referable.

messidor2.note: Krause et al. adjudicated this directly as referable/not-referable using the 1 DD criterion, so 1 here == 2 in IDRiD. Blank/missing = ungradable (4 images), which belongs to referral_or_recapture, NOT to a DME value.

aptos2019.note: No DME labels. primary_referable is NOT scoreable on APTOS - use secondary_dr_only and label it as not comparable to Gulshan/IDx-DR.

primary_referable.name: Referable DR (DR or DME)
primary_referable.rule_note: dme_referable is resolved via the dme_encoding map above, per dataset. It is deliberately NOT a numeric comparison - see amendment 1.1.0 (B12).
primary_referable.rationale: Matches the mtmDR positive class used by IDx-DR (more-than-mild DR and/or clinically significant macular oedema) and the referable class used by Gulshan et al. Krause et al. state it identically: referable DR is 'moderate or worse DR or referable DME'. This is the endpoint the headline Sens/Spec claim is made on.

secondary_dr_only.name: Referable DR (DR grade only)
secondary_dr_only.rationale: Reported alongside the primary endpoint. This is the only endpoint scoreable on APTOS, which ships no DME labels. Not comparable to IDx-DR or Gulshan - state that wherever it appears.

referral_or_recapture.name: Needs a human (referable OR ungradable)
referral_or_recapture.rationale: The endpoint that actually describes our deployed system, because Module 1 can reject an image rather than grade it. Gulshan et al. report this separately and performance drops (AUC 0.991 -> 0.974); ours should be expected to drop too. Reporting only the clean-image endpoint would overstate field performance.

operating_points._policy: Two operating points are selected on the Phase 3 validation split and frozen here BEFORE Messidor-2 is read. Report both, as Gulshan et al. do. A threshold re-tuned after seeing Messidor-2 invalidates the external validation claim.

high_sensitivity.selection_rule: maximise specificity subject to validation sensitivity >= 0.95

operating.selection_rule: maximise Youden J subject to validation sensitivity >= 0.90 and specificity >= 0.85

high_specificity.selection_rule: maximise sensitivity subject to validation specificity >= 0.98

reporting_rules._comment: project hard rule 3 - every reported metric carries its evaluation protocol.
required_with_every_metric: the DME encoding used for that dataset (see dme_encoding)
operating point name and numeric threshold
whether ungradable images were excluded or counted as positive

dme_label_availability.aptos2019: none - DR grade only. Secondary endpoint only.
dme_label_availability.idrid: yes - 'Risk of macular edema' 0/1/2 for all 516 grading images.
dme_label_availability.messidor2: yes - 'adjudicated_dme', binary, in the Krause et al. reference standard (must be downloaded, blocker B1).

ungradable_handling._comment: Messidor-2 ships 4 images the adjudicators could not grade (1748 total, 1744 gradable). They are not a DME value and must not be coerced to 0.
ungradable_handling.rule: Exclude from primary_referable and secondary_dr_only; count as POSITIVE in referral_or_recapture. Always report the gradable denominator alongside the metric.
ungradable_handling.rationale: An image nobody can grade still sends the patient to a human - that is what endpoint 3 measures. Silently dropping these 4 would also make our denominator differ from Gulshan's 1745 without saying so.

implementation_check._comment: B12 was a silent-failure bug: a threshold that matched nothing still produced a plausible-looking number. Guard against the class, not just the instance.
implementation_check.rule: Any code evaluating primary_referable MUST assert that the dataset appears in dme_encoding.per_dataset with a non-null dme_referable, and MUST fail loudly otherwise rather than falling through to a DR-only result.
